paper_title: A Short Proof of Bose--Einstein Condensation in the Gross--Pitaevskii Regime and Beyond (Brennecke, 2025, Annales Henri Poincare)
deeper_reasoning_1:
\textbf{Deeper reasoning 1: Schur-complement renormalization fixes the whole proof architecture.}

\textbf{Claim.}
The two-particle Schur complement does more than replace \(V_N\) by an effective potential. After second quantization and normal ordering, it forces the many-body lower-bound architecture
\[
H_N\geq \mathcal T_c+\mathcal W_{\mathrm{ren}}-R_N,
\qquad
\mathcal T_c:=\sum_{r\in\Lambda^\ast\setminus\{0\}} |r|^2c_r^\ast c_r,
\]
where \(c_r=a_r+d_r\). Thus complete condensation follows once the ground state satisfies
\[
\langle \mathcal T_c\rangle\geq 4\pi^2\langle \mathcal N_+\rangle+o(N),
\qquad
\langle \mathcal W_{\mathrm{ren}}\rangle\geq 4\pi aN^{1+\kappa}+o(N),
\qquad
\langle R_N\rangle=o(N).
\]

\textbf{Premises.}
\[
\begin{array}{ll}
(P1) & H_2=T+V_N,\quad T=-\Delta_{x_1}-\Delta_{x_2},\quad
       D=\Pi_{\mathrm H}H_2\Pi_{\mathrm H}>0.\\[1mm]
(P2) & \displaystyle
       V_{\mathrm{ren}}=N^{1-\kappa}\left(V_N-V_N\Pi_{\mathrm H}D^{-1}\Pi_{\mathrm H}V_N\right),\\[1mm]
(P3) & \displaystyle
       \eta=N^{1-\kappa}\Pi_{\mathrm H}D^{-1}\Pi_{\mathrm H}V_N\Pi_{\mathrm L}.\\[1mm]
(P4) & \displaystyle
       \langle u,H_2u\rangle\geq
       \left\langle \Pi_{\mathrm L}u,
       \left(\Pi_{\mathrm L}T\Pi_{\mathrm L}+N^{\kappa-1}\Pi_{\mathrm L}V_{\mathrm{ren}}\Pi_{\mathrm L}\right)
       \Pi_{\mathrm L}u\right\rangle.\\[2mm]
(P5) & \text{Applying }(P4)\text{ to each pair leaves low--low variables plus the high-sector minimizer encoded by }\eta.\\[1mm]
(P6) & \displaystyle
       d_r=\frac{N^\kappa}{N}\sum_{(p,q)\in P_{\mathrm L}^2}
       \langle \varphi_{p+q-r}\otimes\varphi_r,
       \eta\varphi_p\otimes\varphi_q\rangle a_{p+q-r}^\ast a_pa_q.\\[2mm]
(P7) & \displaystyle
       \mathcal W_{\mathrm{ren}}=\frac{N^\kappa}{2N}
       \sum_{\substack{p,q,r\in\Lambda^\ast\\ p,q,p+r,q-r\in P_{\mathrm L}}}
       \langle\varphi_{p+r}\otimes\varphi_{q-r},V_{\mathrm{ren}}\varphi_p\otimes\varphi_q\rangle
       a_{p+r}^\ast a_{q-r}^\ast a_pa_q.\\[2mm]
(P8) & \text{The remaining normal-ordering and projection errors are collected in a self-adjoint }R_N.
\end{array}
\]

\textbf{Derivation.}
The Schur-complement inequality \((P4)\) has two consequences. First, the low--low part of the pair interaction is no longer governed by the bare potential \(V_N\), but by the resolvent-corrected potential \(V_{\mathrm{ren}}\). Therefore the second-quantized low--low interaction is precisely \(\mathcal W_{\mathrm{ren}}\) from \((P7)\). Second, the high-sector square that was discarded in the two-particle completion of squares leaves its minimizer in the low variables. The coefficients of this minimizer are the matrix elements of \(\eta\), and after writing the kinetic energy in momentum variables they modify the annihilation operators from \(a_r\) to \(c_r=a_r+d_r\), with \(d_r\) as in \((P6)\).

Consequently the many-body lower bound has the form
\begin{align}
H_N
&\geq \sum_{r\in\Lambda^\ast\setminus\{0\}}|r|^2c_r^\ast c_r+
\mathcal W_{\mathrm{ren}}-R_N \\
&=\mathcal T_c+\mathcal W_{\mathrm{ren}}-R_N .
\end{align}
For a normalized ground state \(\psi_N\), write \(\langle A\rangle:=\langle\psi_N,A\psi_N\rangle\). If the three estimates in the claim hold, then
\begin{align}
\langle H_N\rangle
&\geq \langle\mathcal T_c\rangle+\langle\mathcal W_{\mathrm{ren}}\rangle-\langle R_N\rangle\\
&\geq 4\pi^2\langle\mathcal N_+\rangle+4\pi aN^{1+\kappa}+o(N).
\end{align}
Thus the whole proof is reduced to a kinetic positivity problem, a scattering-energy extraction problem, and a remainder-absorption problem.

\textbf{Final Result.}
\[
\boxed{H_N\geq\mathcal T_c+\mathcal W_{\mathrm{ren}}-R_N
\quad\Longrightarrow\quad
\text{BEC follows from the three ground-state estimates above.}}
\]
\hfill$\blacksquare$
deeper_reasoning_3:
\textbf{Deeper reasoning 3: The modified kinetic term recovers the full excitation number.}

\textbf{Claim.}
Assume \(\delta>\kappa/2\), \(\delta<\alpha\), and
\[
\left|\langle\psi_N,E_\delta\psi_N\rangle\right|
\leq C N^{1+3\kappa+\delta/2-7\alpha/2}=o(N).
\]
Then
\[
\left\langle\psi_N,\mathcal T_c\psi_N\right\rangle
\geq 4\pi^2\left\langle\psi_N,\mathcal N_+\psi_N\right\rangle+o(N).
\]

\textbf{Premises.}
\[
\begin{array}{ll}
(P1) & \displaystyle
       \mathcal T_c:=\sum_{r\in\Lambda^\ast\setminus\{0\}}|r|^2c_r^\ast c_r.\\[1mm]
(P2) & \displaystyle
       \mathcal T_c\geq 4\pi^2(\mathcal N_{<N^\delta}-a_0^\ast a_0)+E_\delta.\\[1mm]
(P3) & \displaystyle
       \mathcal N_+=(\mathcal N_{<N^\delta}-a_0^\ast a_0)+\mathcal N_{\geq N^\delta}.\\[1mm]
(P4) & \displaystyle
       \langle\psi_N,\mathcal N_{\geq N^\delta}\psi_N\rangle
       \leq C N^{1+\kappa-2\delta}.\\[1mm]
(P5) & \displaystyle
       \left|\langle\psi_N,E_\delta\psi_N\rangle\right|
       \leq C N^{1+3\kappa+\delta/2-7\alpha/2}=o(N).\\[1mm]
(P6) & \delta>\kappa/2.\\[1mm]
(P7) & N^s=o(N)\text{ whenever }s<1.
\end{array}
\]

\textbf{Derivation.}
The lower bound \((P2)\) controls only the low nonzero modes directly. Using \((P3)\),
\begin{align}
\mathcal N_{<N^\delta}-a_0^\ast a_0
&=\mathcal N_+-\mathcal N_{\geq N^\delta}.
\end{align}
Therefore, in the ground state,
\begin{align}
\langle\mathcal T_c\rangle
&\geq 4\pi^2\langle\mathcal N_+\rangle
      -4\pi^2\langle\mathcal N_{\geq N^\delta}\rangle
      +\langle E_\delta\rangle\\
&\geq 4\pi^2\langle\mathcal N_+\rangle
      -C N^{1+\kappa-2\delta}
      -C N^{1+3\kappa+\delta/2-7\alpha/2}.
\end{align}
The first error is \(o(N)\), because \(\delta>\kappa/2\) gives \(1+\kappa-2\delta<1\). The second error is \(o(N)\) by the stated hypothesis. Hence
\begin{align}
\langle\mathcal T_c\rangle
&\geq 4\pi^2\langle\mathcal N_+\rangle+o(N).
\end{align}
The point is that the modified kinetic term initially sees only modes below \(N^\delta\), but the ordinary kinetic-energy tail estimate upgrades this into a bound for all excitations.

\textbf{Final Result.}
\[
\boxed{\langle\psi_N,\mathcal T_c\psi_N\rangle
\geq 4\pi^2\langle\psi_N,\mathcal N_+\psi_N\rangle+o(N).}
\]
\hfill$\blacksquare$
deeper_reasoning_6:
\textbf{Deeper reasoning 6: One parameter window closes all kinetic, potential, and remainder errors.}

\textbf{Claim.}
For every \(0\leq\kappa<1/20\), the parameters \(\alpha,\beta,\delta\) can be chosen so that all powers
\[
s_1,\ldots,s_5,
\qquad
t_1,
\ldots,t_5
\]
are strictly smaller than \(1\). Hence all kinetic, renormalized-potential, and three-body errors are \(o(N)\).

\textbf{Premises.}
\[
\begin{array}{ll}
(P1) & \displaystyle
s_1=1+\kappa-2\delta,
\quad s_2=1+3\kappa+\delta/2-7\alpha/2,
\quad s_3=5\kappa/2+\delta/2-\alpha.\\[1mm]
(P2) & \displaystyle
s_4=1+2\kappa-2\alpha,
\quad s_5=\kappa+3\alpha.\\[1mm]
(P3) & \displaystyle
t_1=1+5\kappa-2\beta,
\quad t_2=1/2+9\kappa/2+5\alpha/2-2\beta.\\[1mm]
(P4) & \displaystyle
t_3=1+9\kappa/2+\beta/2-3\alpha/2,
\quad t_4=1/2+4\kappa+\alpha+\beta/2.\\[1mm]
(P5) & \displaystyle
t_5=1+4\kappa+5\beta/2-5\alpha/2.\\[1mm]
(P6) & \text{For }0<\kappa<1/20\text{ choose }
       \alpha=(1+\varepsilon)\frac{41}{10}\kappa,
       \quad \beta=(1+\varepsilon)\frac52\kappa,\\
     & \text{and choose }\delta\text{ with }\kappa/2<\delta<\alpha,\text{ sufficiently close to }\kappa/2.\\[1mm]
(P7) & \text{For }\kappa=0\text{ choose }0<\beta<\delta<\alpha<1/5\text{ with the inequalities below strict.}\\[1mm]
(P8) & N^s=o(N)\text{ whenever }s<1.
\end{array}
\]

\textbf{Derivation.}
First take \(0<\kappa<1/20\). At \(\varepsilon=0\) and \(\delta=\kappa/2\), the kinetic and potential exponents have the values
\begin{align}
s_1&=1,\\
s_2&=1+3\kappa+\kappa/4-\frac72\frac{41}{10}\kappa=1-\frac{111}{10}\kappa<1,\\
s_3&=\frac52\kappa+\frac14\kappa-\frac{41}{10}\kappa=-\frac{27}{20}\kappa<1,\\
s_4&=1+2\kappa-2\frac{41}{10}\kappa=1-\frac{31}{5}\kappa<1,\\
s_5&=\kappa+3\frac{41}{10}\kappa=\frac{133}{10}\kappa<1.
\end{align}
The equality \(s_1=1\) is made strict by choosing \(\delta>\kappa/2\). The three-body exponents at \(\varepsilon=0\) are
\begin{align}
t_1&=1,\\
t_2&=\frac12+\frac92\kappa+\frac52\frac{41}{10}\kappa-5\kappa
    =\frac12+\frac{39}{4}\kappa<1,\\
t_3&=1+\frac92\kappa+\frac12\frac52\kappa-\frac32\frac{41}{10}\kappa
    =1-\frac25\kappa<1,\\
t_4&=\frac12+4\kappa+\frac{41}{10}\kappa+\frac12\frac52\kappa
    =\frac12+\frac{187}{20}\kappa<1,\\
t_5&=1+4\kappa+\frac52\frac52\kappa-\frac52\frac{41}{10}\kappa
    =1-\frac12\kappa<1.
\end{align}
The equality \(t_1=1\) is made strict by taking \(\varepsilon>0\), because then
\begin{align}
t_1=1+5\kappa-5(1+\varepsilon)\kappa=1-5\varepsilon\kappa<1.
\end{align}
All other strict inequalities remain strict for sufficiently small \(\varepsilon>0\) and \(\delta\) sufficiently close to \(\kappa/2\), by continuity.

For \(\kappa=0\), choose \(0<\beta<\delta<\alpha<1/5\) with \(\beta\) close enough to \(\alpha\) where needed. Then
\begin{align}
s_1&=1-2\delta<1,
& s_2&=1+\delta/2-7\alpha/2<1,
& s_3&=\delta/2-\alpha<1,\\
s_4&=1-2\alpha<1,
& s_5&=3\alpha<1,
& t_1&=1-2\beta<1,\\
t_2&=1/2+5\alpha/2-2\beta<1,
& t_3&=1+\beta/2-3\alpha/2<1,
& t_4&=1/2+\alpha+\beta/2<1,\\
t_5&=1+5\beta/2-5\alpha/2<1.
\end{align}
Therefore every listed exponent is below \(1\), and \((P8)\) converts every corresponding power into \(o(N)\).

\textbf{Final Result.}
\[
\boxed{0\leq\kappa<1/20
\quad\Longrightarrow\quad
N^{s_j}=o(N),\ N^{t_j}=o(N)\text{ for all }j.}
\]
\hfill$\blacksquare$
